messages:
Sylvia Park: heads-up — we saw a recurring tail-latency spike in prod around 18:00 UTC tied to KV cache churn. pattern looks like a short eviction storm then a thundering repopulate. not just higher p99, entire request profiles show extra 30-80ms from pager activity.
Kevin Liu: yup noticed that too. traces point to lots of `kv_page_fault` events and a burst of `evict` ops. queue length on the pager thread shot up.
Maria Gonzales: any repro? or a specific model/seq-len distribution?
Sylvia Park: seems most visible on long-context chat workloads (avg seq 4k+). also when we switch to the FIFO fallback under memory pressure. FIFO seems to cause more frequent reinsert churn in our workload.
Alex Chen: interesting — FIFO should be cheaper to maintain but may evict prefixes that are still hot for streaming. LRU keeps hot prefixes but heavier to update. could be lock contention on LRU maintenance.
Kevin Liu: i pulled profiler snapshot from canary around the spike, put numbers below. not pretty.
perf-bot: profiler snapshot 1865432330 attached.
Kevin Liu: ```
# sample counters (canary run)
kv_evictions_total: 12432
kv_reinserts_total: 4821
kv_page_faults: 1190
pager_queue_ms_p99: 78
pager_lock_wait_ms_avg: 2.6
thread_ksvc_cpu_pct: 34
```
Maria Gonzales: Oof — reinserts ~40% of evictions. that explains the memory growth + extra work. any evidence of correctness issues (dup keys / stale pointers)?
Sylvia Park: we saw one dubious stack from a dev-run where reinsert ordering led to stale `kv_ref` being used transiently, but GC eventually fixed it. not a crash but could amplify latency.
Alex Chen: can you paste a short log slice where it spikes? looking for interleaved evict/reinsert around same key ranges.
Kevin Liu: pasted below (sensitive redacted):
```
[18:02:11.112] KV: evict key=ctx:usr:1234 shard=5 size=48
[18:02:11.113] KV: reinsert key=ctx:usr:1234 shard=5 reason=stream-resume
[18:02:11.113] PAGer: page_in shard=5 offset=0..128 (fault)
[18:02:11.115] KV: evict key=ctx:usr:1234 shard=5 size=48
[18:02:11.116] KV: reinsert key=ctx:usr:1234 shard=5 reason=tooling
[18:02:11.117] PAGer: page_in shard=5 offset=128..256 (fault)
```
Maria Gonzales: that pattern (evict immediately followed by reinsert) is the classic thundering—multiple requests are streaming same prefix concurrently and FIFO bumped one of them out so others repopulate. under LRU we'd keep the most recently used but update cost may be the source of lock waits.
Alex Chen: hypothesis: under high concurrency, our FIFO implementation performs well until a particular shard gets many streaming clients. then eviction bursts + reinserts cause pager thrash and lock contention, manifesting as latency spikes. also possible race where reinsert path touches a weak pointer that wasn't fully cleared leading to transient stale access.
Sylvia Park: agree. quick mitigation options: 1) raise shard cache watermark temporarily, 2) add short grace period before evicting recently pop'ed keys (reinsert suppression), or 3) prefer LRU for hot shards.
Kevin Liu: i ran a small micro-repro on staging: `scripts/kv_thundering_repro.sh --clients 60 --seq 6k --shard 5` — reproduces p99 bump reliably. attached CPU + flamegraph.
Maria Gonzales: can we add an atomic reinsert counter so we can avoid double-work? like compare-and-swap on slot state and short-circuit if another thread already repopulated. cheap and correct.
Alex Chen: that sounds safe. also consider batching reinserts — if many clients request same prefix, let one fetcher populate and others wait on its future. similar to singleflight.
Sylvia Park: agree on singleflight. also we should add an integration test that simulates concurrent streaming clients on same shard to assert no more than N page fetches per prefix in window.
Kevin Liu: i'll prototype singleflight + CAS optimization in a branch. perf-bot will run smoke.
perf-bot: running smoke tests on branch kv/singleflight-cas-186543 — ETA 6m.
Maria Gonzales: for canary plan: roll 10% on dedicated, monitor `kv_reinserts_total`, `pager_queue_ms_p99`, and `evict_rate`. if p99 drops and reinserts fall >50% then promote. if errors >0.1% abort.
Alex Chen: good plan. also add a quick heap snapshot after canary to detect memory growth regression.
Sylvia Park: assigning Kevin for patch, Maria to own canary, Alex to add integration test. target deploy tomorrow morning.
Kevin Liu: started PR draft, linking test + perf numbers. will ping when ready for review. :thumbsup:
deploy-bot: scheduled canary deploy at 06:00 UTC to cluster-rw-3 (traffic 10%).
Sylvia Park: thanks all — main priority is correctness (no stale pointer use) + reduce thundering. we'll keep LRU/FIFO discussion separate, but short-term singleflight + CAS should mitigate the worst-case latency. follow-up: we should eventually benchmark LRU maintenance overhead vs FIFO thundering on representative workloads.
Alex Chen: filing a follow-up perf story for kernel-selection/batching interactions — KV behavior affects batching latency significantly. linking later.
Maria Gonzales: ack, will add metrics dashboard tiles for `kv_reinserts_total` and `prefix_fetch_inflight` so we can visualize during rollout.
Sylvia Park: closing loop here. will update thread with PR + canary results. :white_check_mark:
